title: Where to park and how far to walk on the Tanglefoot Trail this Thanksgiving in Pontotoc
excerpt: The trail district’s regular hours give Pontotoc roughly 6:09 a.m. to 5:17 p.m. on Thanksgiving. The Algoma and Ecru stops are each under seven miles from town.
locality: Pontotoc Gateway and the Algoma and Ecru whistle stops in Pontotoc County, Mississippi.

facts.statement: Families taking a Thanksgiving walk or bike ride on the Tanglefoot Trail can start in downtown Pontotoc and head toward either Algoma or Ecru. The trail district’s regular hours work out to about 6:09 a.m. to 5:17 p.m. in Pontotoc on Thursday, Nov. 26. Posted restrictions at an entrance take precedence.
facts.evidence: District rule allows 30 minutes before sunrise to 30 minutes after sunset unless otherwise posted. The Naval Observatory gives 06:39 and 16:47 CST for coordinates near downtown Pontotoc.

paragraphs.text: Families taking a Thanksgiving walk or bike ride on the Tanglefoot Trail can start in downtown Pontotoc and head toward either Algoma or Ecru. The trail district’s regular hours work out to about 6:09 a.m. to 5:17 p.m. in Pontotoc on Thursday, Nov. 26. Posted restrictions at an entrance take precedence.

For the downtown gateway, the district directs visitors to park at the Pontotoc Gas System warehouse, 140 W. Reynolds St. The town is at mile 25.8. Heading south, the Algoma Whistle Stop is 6½ miles away at mile 19.3. Going north instead, Ecru is 6.8 miles away at mile 32.6. Those distances are one way.

The whistle stops also give families a place to start closer to home. For Algoma, the district lists 24 Weeks St., with Pontotoc as the mailing city. For Ecru, use 279 S. Railroad Ave. Visitors may enter from public roads and designated access points and should use marked parking areas.

The trail district sets its hours by the sun seven days a week. The Naval Observatory gives a 6:39 a.m. sunrise and a 4:47 p.m. sunset for Pontotoc on Thanksgiving. Children younger than 12 need an adult with them on district property, and dogs must be leashed and accompanied by their owners.
